documents.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
documents.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. documents.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
documents.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. documents.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
documents.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n

documents.title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
documents.abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. documents.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
documents.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat

documents.title: Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy.
documents.abstract: Single-cell Assay for Transposase Accessible Chromatin with sequencing (scATAC-seq) is widely used to investigate chromatin accessibility but experiments often contain empty droplets, droplets containing damaged nuclei or cellular-debris. Accurately filtering high-quality nuclei is important as noisy droplets contribute reads that can distort downstream analysis and obscure rare cell population. Current approaches often rely on read depth and or predefined genomic features that are not exactly the same as chromatin accessibility landscape. documents.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
documents.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. documents.title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. documents.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
documents.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. documents.title: SigBridgeR: An R Toolkit for Standardized Identification and Benchmarking of Phenotype-Associated Cell Subpopulations in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, yet linking specific cell subpopulations to clinically relevant phenotypes remains a major challenge. documents.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. documents.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. documents.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
documents.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod

documents.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.

documents.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
documents.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.

documents.title: Decoding pyroptosis at single-cell resolution: heterogeneity, microenvironment remodeling and potential translational insights.
documents.abstract: Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory programmed cell death mediated by inflammatory caspases and Gasdermin (GSDM) family proteins, exerts dual roles in host defense and pathological damage. Traditional bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) is limited in capturing single-cell heterogeneity and dissecting intercellular communication, impeding in-depth mechanistic exploration of pyroptosis. documents.title: Reanalysis of public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomes identifies widespread tumor-normal dysregulation and a cross-layer cell-cycle signal in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma.
documents.abstract: Sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC) is a rare malignancy affecting the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection identified as a critical etiological factor in a subset of cases. HPV-positive and HPV-negative SNSCC exhibit distinct clinical behaviors, with HPV-positive tumors generally demonstrating better prognosis and treatment response. However, the cellular composition and transcriptomic landscape of SNSCC tumor versus normal tissue remain incompletely characterized. documents.title: Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.
documents.abstract: Predicting single-gene knockout effects from wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging when perturbation experiments are costly and existing approaches require knockout-specific model training. Here we introduce Topology-Adjusted Knockout (TAKO), a computationally efficient WT-only framework for single-gene KO impact ranking on single-cell gene regulatory networks.
